title: Pangram Check: Public Pass, Private Miss, Then Fix
description: A student repeatedly gets close, hits private-test edge cases, and eventually closes the gap.
why_interesting: Classic “public tests pass but private tests fail” journey, with visible recovery and final success.

timeline.text: Problem setup: determine whether a sentence is a pangram (contains every letter). The student starts close but not fully correct.
First visible wobble: a runtime error appears. They may be thinking, “I broke something simple while trying to patch logic.”
Long stretch of local edits: still stuck around partial public correctness. This is a pattern of patching symptoms, not yet the rule.
Big moment: all public tests pass. It looks done, but this is often a false summit.
Immediately after that, private tests fail. Hidden cases expose an assumption that public tests did not challenge.
Another loop: public looks green again, private is still unstable. They may be checking outputs instead of re-checking the core condition.
Breakthrough: private tests finally pass. The underlying logic is now robust, not just sample-friendly.
Final submission succeeds (100). This replay is useful for teaching why hidden-edge reasoning matters.
